dedupe_keys.name: urban form toronto built environment and walkability measures on a 100 m hexagon grid

description: This repository generates measures of urban form, built environment and walkability for the Toronto region, the Greater Golden Horseshoe, from open sources such as OpenStreetMap and Statistics Canada. Measures sit on a hexagonal grid with a 100 m apothem, 200 m between centroids, and are also interpolated to 2016 dissemination areas and traffic analysis zones. They are 2016 population and employment density from the census, business density from the Canadian business registry, counts of three-way and four-way intersections, walking network length from OpenStreetMap and transit trips per hour from GTFS, all as of December 2018. It was produced by the SAUSy Lab with PostGIS, Python and command line tools. Coverage: Greater Golden Horseshoe, Ontario. Access: free on GitHub; the grid file is linked from Dropbox. Licence: MIT. Caveats: 2016 to 2018 inputs; last commit July 2020. Simulation uses are exposure of population and jobs and walkable access in hazard and service studies. Related records: the global urban form metrics for 462 cities and the EPA National Walkability Index.
name: Urban Form Toronto: built environment and walkability measures on a 100 m hexagon grid
